title: Learning to Reach Goals via Diffusion

en.text: In offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning, we want an agent to reach any target state from any starting point, learning purely from a batch of pre-collected data. The reward is usually sparse: 1 when the goal is reached, 0 otherwise. The setting is practical, and it is also stubbornly hard.

Most methods first learn a value function and then improve a policy against it. Offline, that first step is fragile. The policy proposes actions that never appear in the data, the value function scores those actions incorrectly, and the errors compound over time until the policy diverges. Sparse binary rewards only make the estimation problem harder.

This ICML 2024 paper, from McGill University and Mila, takes a different angle. If we treat goal states as the data distribution we want to model, is reaching a goal really so different from denoising in a diffusion model? Their method, Merlin, constructs trajectories that drift step by step away from the goal, then trains a policy to reverse that drift, with no value function anywhere in the loop.

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea behind Merlin. Just as image diffusion turns Gaussian noise back into a real sample, Merlin builds trajectories that walk away from the goal (grey dotted arrows, forward diffusion), then learns a goal-conditioned policy to reverse them (green solid arrows, reverse diffusion), reaching the goal from an arbitrary initial state.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02505  |  Code: https://github.com/vineetjain96/merlin
Why value functions struggle here

Online reinforcement learning can keep interacting with the environment and correct a bad value estimate. Offline, it cannot: once the dataset is fixed, the agent never receives new feedback. To stabilize offline learning, prior work typically constrains the policy or uses conservative value updates, but those fixes tend to cost performance and generalization. Underneath it all is a more basic question: do we actually need to estimate how good each state is at all?

Diffusion models are a working example of an answer that says no. A forward process gradually corrupts data into Gaussian noise, and a learned reverse process denoises it back into realistic samples, without ever estimating a value function. That analogy is exactly Merlin's starting point: noise is a walk away from the data manifold, and in goal-conditioned RL we can likewise construct trajectories that walk away from a goal, then learn to reverse them.
Merlin: goal-conditioned RL as reverse diffusion

Concretely: take a trajectory from the offline dataset and read it backwards, starting from its final goal state. Applying a forward diffusion transformation at each step produces a sequence of states that drift progressively away from the goal, exactly like adding noise in an image diffusion model. What Merlin learns is the goal-conditioned policy that reverses this drift, one step at a time.

en.caption: Figure 2. Forward and reverse diffusion for goal-conditioned RL, illustrated on a 2D navigation task. The star is the goal state; red dotted arrows are the forward transitions q(s_t|s_{t+1}), and green arrows the reverse transitions P^{pi_theta}(s_{t+1}|s_t). The policy learns the green direction.

en.text: The key theoretical result is that maximizing the log-likelihood of goal states under this reverse process reduces to plain behavior cloning on hindsight-relabeled data. The value function drops out entirely, and the training objective collapses to a single supervised-learning expression. Just as important, because the diffusion happens directly in the state space, the policy needs only 1 denoising iteration per environment step, instead of the many iterations a typical diffusion policy runs. That is where Merlin's speed and stability come from.
Three ways to walk away from the goal

How you construct the forward trajectory determines what the policy has to reverse, and Merlin offers three constructions, one per variant. The base Merlin uses a fixed heuristic rule to generate goal-departing trajectories; Merlin-P replaces the forward process with a learned parametric forward model; and Merlin-NP takes a non-parametric route, retrieving nearest neighbors in a learned latent space and stitching nearby states together.

That stitching is what makes Merlin-NP stronger. Because nearest neighbors are computed in the learned latent space, connected states are genuinely close in a meaningful sense, so the reverse policy can compose sub-segments from different trajectories into a new route to the goal, even one that never appears as a single trajectory in the data.

en.caption: Figure 3. Trajectory stitching: nearest neighbors are computed in the learned latent space so that connected states sit close together (left), letting the reverse policy join two sub-trajectories into one coherent path to the goal (right). This lets Merlin-NP reach beyond the coverage of any single demonstration.

en.text: Does it work?

The authors evaluate on the offline goal-conditioned benchmark of Yang et al. (2021): 10 control tasks, from simple point navigation and Reacher to harder Fetch push, pick, and slide, plus the high-dimensional HandReach. Every task uses a sparse binary reward and a maximum trajectory length T = 50, and results are averaged across expert and random datasets over 10 random seeds. The baselines span goal-conditioned RL methods (GCSL, WGCSL, AM, GoFAR) and diffusion-based methods (Decision Diffuser, g-DQL, BESO).

en.caption: Figure 4. Benchmark tasks (top), normalized returns (left), and log inference time (right). Merlin, Merlin-P, and Merlin-NP (blue, boxed in red) match or exceed every baseline on returns while running about an order of magnitude (10×) faster than the diffusion methods (DD, BESO).

en.text: The picture is consistent. Base Merlin already beats the baselines on most tasks, and Merlin-P and Merlin-NP push returns higher still. Measured by average rank across all 10 methods and 10 tasks, Merlin-NP comes out on top, with an average rank around 1.7 on state observations and about 1.25 on pixel observations. And because it performs a single denoising step per environment step, its training and inference run roughly 10× faster than diffusion methods like Decision Diffuser and BESO. The higher-dimensional the observation, such as pixel input, the larger that speed gap grows.

en.caption: Table 1. The three Merlin variants and how each constructs its forward (goal-departing) trajectory.
rows: Non-parametric nearest-neighbor stitching in latent space

en.text: How far ahead to aim

Merlin has two main tunable hyperparameters: the hindsight-relabeling ratio and the evaluation time horizon h, which sets how far ahead the policy aims at each step. The authors sweep h systematically and plot the outcome as heatmaps.

en.caption: Figure 5. Relative discounted returns per task across evaluation horizons h (left: expert dataset; right: random dataset). Conditioning on some horizon consistently beats not conditioning (the None column), and the best h shifts with task difficulty: easier tasks favor short horizons, and HandReach in particular works well only at h=1.

en.text: Two things stand out. First, conditioning on a time horizon almost always beats not conditioning at all (the rightmost None column is visibly lighter). Second, the best horizon depends on the task: an easy task like PointReach does well at a short horizon (h=1 or h=5), while harder tasks need longer ones, with the sweep spanning roughly {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}. HandReach is the most sensitive of all, working only at h=1. So Merlin is broadly robust to the horizon choice, though a few high-dimensional tasks still need task-specific tuning.
Takeaway and limits

The point worth remembering is that Merlin rewrites offline goal-conditioned RL as the reverse of a diffusion process, and that rewrite makes the problem remarkably simple. Construct trajectories that walk away from goals, learn to reverse them, and goal-reaching collapses into ordinary behavior cloning, with no value function to estimate and no attendant instability to fight. It matches or beats state-of-the-art methods across 10 tasks while running about an order of magnitude faster than other diffusion-based approaches.

The framework does come with conditions. It targets the offline, sparse-reward, goal-conditioned setting; the choice of forward-trajectory construction (fixed, parametric, or non-parametric stitching) has to be matched to the task, and a few high-dimensional tasks such as HandReach remain sensitive to hyperparameters like the horizon. But performing diffusion directly in the state space, with a single denoising step per environment step, is what makes diffusion for RL look, for the first time, both simple and scalable, and that may matter more than any single benchmark number.

zh.text: 在离线目标条件强化学习（offline goal-conditioned RL）中，我们希望智能体只依靠一批预先收集好的数据，就能学会从任意起点到达任意目标。奖励往往是稀疏的：到达目标记 1，否则记 0。这个设定很实用，却也很棘手。
大多数方法的做法是先学一个价值函数（value function），再据此改进策略。但在离线设定下，这一步格外脆弱：策略会尝试数据中从未出现过的动作，价值函数对这些动作给出错误估计，误差在时间上不断累积，最终可能让策略彻底发散。稀疏奖励只会让估计更难。
这篇 ICML 2024 论文（作者来自 McGill University 与 Mila）换了一个角度：如果把目标状态看成我们想要建模的数据分布，那么「到达目标」是不是就等价于扩散模型里的「去噪」？他们提出的方法 Merlin，先构造出一批逐步远离目标的轨迹，再训练一个策略把这个过程反转回来，全程不需要价值函数。

zh.caption: 图1 本文方法 Merlin 的核心思想：正如图像扩散把高斯噪声一步步还原成真实样本，Merlin 先构造出从目标「走开」的轨迹（灰色虚线，前向扩散），再学习一个目标条件策略把它们反转（绿色实线，反向扩散），从而能从任意初始状态回到目标。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02505 ｜ 代码：https://github.com/vineetjain96/merlin
为什么价值函数在这里靠不住
在线强化学习可以不断与环境交互、纠正错误的价值估计；离线设定却不行——数据一旦固定，智能体就再也拿不到新的反馈。为了稳住离线学习，已有工作通常给策略加约束，或者采用更保守的价值更新，但这些手段往往以牺牲性能和泛化为代价。问题的根源其实是一个更基本的追问：我们究竟需不需要显式地去估计「每个状态到底有多好」？
扩散模型给出了一个「不需要」的样板。它先用一个前向过程把数据一点点破坏成高斯噪声，再学习一个反向过程，把噪声重新去噪成真实样本——整个过程从头到尾都没有价值函数。Merlin 的出发点正是这个类比：噪声是「走离」数据流形的过程，而在目标条件强化学习里，我们同样可以构造出「走离」目标的轨迹，然后学着把它反转。
Merlin：把目标条件强化学习写成反向扩散
具体怎么做？取数据集里的一条轨迹，从它的最终目标状态开始倒着看。在每一步施加一个前向扩散变换，就会得到一串逐渐远离目标的状态，正如图像扩散里逐步加噪。Merlin 要学的，就是把这个漂移一步步反转回去的目标条件策略。

zh.caption: 图2 以 2D 导航为例的前向与反向扩散过程。星号是目标状态；红色虚线箭头表示前向过程的状态转移 q(s_t|s_{t+1})，绿色箭头表示反向过程 P^{π_θ}(s_{t+1}|s_t)。策略要学的正是绿色箭头这一方向。

zh.text: 论文的关键理论结果是：在这个反向扩散过程下最大化目标状态的对数似然，等价于在经过事后重标注（hindsight relabeling）的数据上做普通的行为克隆（behavior cloning）。换句话说，价值函数被彻底省掉了，训练目标简化成一条监督学习式的公式。更关键的是，由于扩散直接发生在状态空间里，策略每走一步环境只需要 1 次去噪迭代，而不像典型扩散策略那样每一步都要迭代很多次——这正是 Merlin 又快又稳的来源。
三种「走离目标」的方式
前向轨迹如何构造，直接决定了策略要反转的是什么。Merlin 给出了三种方案，对应三个变体。最基础的 Merlin 用一个固定的启发式规则生成远离目标的轨迹；Merlin-P 把前向过程换成一个可学习的参数化模型（parametric forward model）；Merlin-NP 则采用非参数（non-parametric）的做法——在学到的隐空间里做最近邻检索，把彼此邻近的状态拼接起来。
Merlin-NP 的拼接（stitching）是它更强的关键。因为最近邻是在学到的隐空间里计算的，被连接的状态在语义上彼此靠近，于是反向策略可以把不同轨迹的子段组合起来，拼出一条通向目标的新路径——即使这条完整路径从未在数据中出现过。

zh.caption: 图3 轨迹拼接：在学到的隐空间中计算最近邻，使被连接的状态彼此邻近（左），从而让反向策略把两条子轨迹拼成一条通向目标的连贯路径（右）。这让 Merlin-NP 能超出单条示范轨迹的覆盖范围。

zh.text: 效果到底如何

作者在 Yang 等人（2021）的离线目标条件基准上评测，一共 10 个控制任务，从简单的点导航、Reacher，到更难的 Fetch 抓取、推动、滑动，以及高维的 HandReach。每个任务都用稀疏二值奖励、最大轨迹长度 T=50，并在「专家」与「随机」两种数据集上、跨 10 个随机种子取平均。对比对象既包括目标条件强化学习基线（GCSL、WGCSL、AM、GoFAR），也包括扩散类方法（Decision Diffuser、g-DQL、BESO）。

zh.caption: 图4 基准任务（上）、归一化回报（左）与对数推理时间（右）。Merlin、Merlin-P、Merlin-NP（蓝色，红框标出）在回报上追平或超过所有基线，同时推理速度比扩散类方法（DD、BESO）快约一个数量级（10×）。

zh.text: 结论相当一致：最基础的 Merlin 就已经在多数任务上胜过基线，Merlin-P 与 Merlin-NP 进一步把回报推高。以在全部 10 个方法、10 个任务上的平均排名来衡量，Merlin-NP 综合最优——在状态观测下平均排名约 1.7，在像素观测下约 1.25。而由于每步只做一次去噪，它的训练和推理都比 Decision Diffuser、BESO 这类扩散方法快约 10×；观测维度越高（例如像素输入），这个速度差距还会进一步拉大。

zh.caption: 表1 三个 Merlin 变体及其前向轨迹的构造方式。
rows: 可学习的参数化前向模型
隐空间最近邻拼接（非参数）

zh.text: 该往前看多远
Merlin 有两个主要的可调超参数：事后重标注的比例，以及评测时的时间视野 h（策略每一步瞄准多远的目标）。作者系统地扫描了 h 的取值，并把结果画成热力图。

zh.caption: 图5 不同评测视野 h 下各任务的相对折扣回报（左：专家数据集；右：随机数据集）。总体上「条件于某个视野」都优于「不条件」（None 列），且最优 h 随任务难度变化：简单任务偏好短视野，HandReach 尤其明显，只有在 h=1 时才表现良好。

zh.text: 从热力图可以读出两点。其一，条件于一个时间视野，几乎总是优于完全不条件（最右侧 None 列颜色更浅）。其二，最优视野取决于任务：像 PointReach 这样简单的任务，在短视野（h=1 或 h=5）下就很好，而更难的任务需要更长的视野；扫描范围大致覆盖 {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}。HandReach 是最敏感的一个——只有在 h=1 时才有效。这说明 Merlin 对视野的选择整体是稳健的，但个别高维任务仍需针对性调参。
小结与边界
Merlin 最值得记住的一点，是它把离线目标条件强化学习重写成了一个扩散过程的逆过程，而这个重写让问题变得异常简单：构造出远离目标的轨迹、再学着反转它们，目标到达就退化成了普通的行为克隆——没有价值函数要估计，也没有随之而来的不稳定要对抗。它在 10 个任务上追平或超过当前最好的方法，却比其它扩散类方法快约一个数量级。
当然，这套框架也有它的前提。它面向的是离线、稀疏奖励、目标条件的设定；前向轨迹的构造方式（固定、参数化，或非参数拼接）需要按任务选择，个别高维任务（如 HandReach）对视野等超参数仍然敏感。但把扩散直接放在状态空间、每步只做一次去噪这一点，让「用扩散来做强化学习」第一次显得既简单又可扩展——这也许比某个具体分数更值得关注。

具体怎么做？取数据集里的一条轨迹，从它的最终目标状态开始倒着看。在每一步施加一个前向扩散变换，就会得到一串逐渐远离目标的状态，正如图像扩散里逐步加噪。Merlin 要学的，就是把这个漂移一步步反转回去的目标条件策略。

zh.caption: 图2 以 2D 导航为例的前向与反向扩散过程。星号是目标状态；红色虚线箭头表示前向过程的状态转移 q(s_t|s_{t+1})，绿色箭头表示反向过程 P^{π_θ}(s_{t+1}|s_t)。策略要学的正是绿色箭头这一方向。

zh.text: 论文的关键理论结果是：在这个反向扩散过程下最大化目标状态的对数似然，等价于在经过事后重标注（hindsight relabeling）的数据上做普通的行为克隆（behavior cloning）。换句话说，价值函数被彻底省掉了，训练目标简化成一条监督学习式的公式。更关键的是，由于扩散直接发生在状态空间里，策略每走一步环境只需要 1 次去噪迭代，而不像典型扩散策略那样每一步都要迭代很多次——这正是 Merlin 又快又稳的来源。

en.title: ICML 2024 | Reaching a Goal Is Just Diffusion, Run in Reverse
en.subtitle: McGill and Mila propose Merlin, a value-function-free method for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 把「到达目标」看成扩散过程的逆过程
zh.subtitle: McGill 与 Mila 提出 Merlin：一个不需要价值函数的目标条件强化学习方法

en.text: In offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning, we want an agent to reach any target state from any starting point, learning purely from a batch of pre-collected data. The reward is usually sparse: 1 when the goal is reached, 0 otherwise. The setting is practical, and it is also stubbornly hard.

Most methods first learn a value function and then improve a policy against it. Offline, that first step is fragile. The policy proposes actions that never appear in the data, the value function scores those actions incorrectly, and the errors compound over time until the policy diverges. Sparse binary rewards only make the estimation problem harder.

This ICML 2024 paper, from McGill University and Mila, takes a different angle. If we treat goal states as the data distribution we want to model, is reaching a goal really so different from denoising in a diffusion model? Their method, Merlin, constructs trajectories that drift step by step away from the goal, then trains a policy to reverse that drift, with no value function anywhere in the loop.

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea behind Merlin. Just as image diffusion turns Gaussian noise back into a real sample, Merlin builds trajectories that walk away from the goal (grey dotted arrows, forward diffusion), then learns a goal-conditioned policy to reverse them (green solid arrows, reverse diffusion), reaching the goal from an arbitrary initial state.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02505  |  Code: https://github.com/vineetjain96/merlin
Does it work?

The authors evaluate on the offline goal-conditioned benchmark of Yang et al. (2021): 10 control tasks, from simple point navigation and Reacher to harder Fetch push, pick, and slide, plus the high-dimensional HandReach. Every task uses a sparse binary reward and a maximum trajectory length T = 50, and results are averaged across expert and random datasets over 10 random seeds. The baselines span goal-conditioned RL methods (GCSL, WGCSL, AM, GoFAR) and diffusion-based methods (Decision Diffuser, g-DQL, BESO).

en.caption: Figure 4. Benchmark tasks (top), normalized returns (left), and log inference time (right). Merlin, Merlin-P, and Merlin-NP (blue, boxed in red) match or exceed every baseline on returns while running about an order of magnitude (10×) faster than the diffusion methods (DD, BESO).

en.text: The picture is consistent. Base Merlin already beats the baselines on most tasks, and Merlin-P and Merlin-NP push returns higher still. Measured by average rank across all 10 methods and 10 tasks, Merlin-NP comes out on top, with an average rank around 1.7 on state observations and about 1.25 on pixel observations. And because it performs a single denoising step per environment step, its training and inference run roughly 10× faster than diffusion methods like Decision Diffuser and BESO. The higher-dimensional the observation, such as pixel input, the larger that speed gap grows.

rows: Non-parametric nearest-neighbor stitching in latent space

zh.text: 在离线目标条件强化学习（offline goal-conditioned RL）中，我们希望智能体只依靠一批预先收集好的数据，就能学会从任意起点到达任意目标。奖励往往是稀疏的：到达目标记 1，否则记 0。这个设定很实用，却也很棘手。
大多数方法的做法是先学一个价值函数（value function），再据此改进策略。但在离线设定下，这一步格外脆弱：策略会尝试数据中从未出现过的动作，价值函数对这些动作给出错误估计，误差在时间上不断累积，最终可能让策略彻底发散。稀疏奖励只会让估计更难。
这篇 ICML 2024 论文（作者来自 McGill University 与 Mila）换了一个角度：如果把目标状态看成我们想要建模的数据分布，那么「到达目标」是不是就等价于扩散模型里的「去噪」？他们提出的方法 Merlin，先构造出一批逐步远离目标的轨迹，再训练一个策略把这个过程反转回来，全程不需要价值函数。

zh.caption: 图1 本文方法 Merlin 的核心思想：正如图像扩散把高斯噪声一步步还原成真实样本，Merlin 先构造出从目标「走开」的轨迹（灰色虚线，前向扩散），再学习一个目标条件策略把它们反转（绿色实线，反向扩散），从而能从任意初始状态回到目标。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02505 ｜ 代码：https://github.com/vineetjain96/merlin
效果到底如何

作者在 Yang 等人（2021）的离线目标条件基准上评测，一共 10 个控制任务，从简单的点导航、Reacher，到更难的 Fetch 抓取、推动、滑动，以及高维的 HandReach。每个任务都用稀疏二值奖励、最大轨迹长度 T=50，并在「专家」与「随机」两种数据集上、跨 10 个随机种子取平均。对比对象既包括目标条件强化学习基线（GCSL、WGCSL、AM、GoFAR），也包括扩散类方法（Decision Diffuser、g-DQL、BESO）。

zh.caption: 图4 基准任务（上）、归一化回报（左）与对数推理时间（右）。Merlin、Merlin-P、Merlin-NP（蓝色，红框标出）在回报上追平或超过所有基线，同时推理速度比扩散类方法（DD、BESO）快约一个数量级（10×）。

zh.text: 结论相当一致：最基础的 Merlin 就已经在多数任务上胜过基线，Merlin-P 与 Merlin-NP 进一步把回报推高。以在全部 10 个方法、10 个任务上的平均排名来衡量，Merlin-NP 综合最优——在状态观测下平均排名约 1.7，在像素观测下约 1.25。而由于每步只做一次去噪，它的训练和推理都比 Decision Diffuser、BESO 这类扩散方法快约 10×；观测维度越高（例如像素输入），这个速度差距还会进一步拉大。

zh.caption: 表1 三个 Merlin 变体及其前向轨迹的构造方式。
rows: 可学习的参数化前向模型

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea behind Merlin. Just as image diffusion turns Gaussian noise back into a real sample, Merlin builds trajectories that walk away from the goal (grey dotted arrows, forward diffusion), then learns a goal-conditioned policy to reverse them (green solid arrows, reverse diffusion), reaching the goal from an arbitrary initial state.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02505  |  Code: https://github.com/vineetjain96/merlin
Merlin: goal-conditioned RL as reverse diffusion

Concretely: take a trajectory from the offline dataset and read it backwards, starting from its final goal state. Applying a forward diffusion transformation at each step produces a sequence of states that drift progressively away from the goal, exactly like adding noise in an image diffusion model. What Merlin learns is the goal-conditioned policy that reverses this drift, one step at a time.

en.caption: Figure 2. Forward and reverse diffusion for goal-conditioned RL, illustrated on a 2D navigation task. The star is the goal state; red dotted arrows are the forward transitions q(s_t|s_{t+1}), and green arrows the reverse transitions P^{pi_theta}(s_{t+1}|s_t). The policy learns the green direction.

en.text: The key theoretical result is that maximizing the log-likelihood of goal states under this reverse process reduces to plain behavior cloning on hindsight-relabeled data. The value function drops out entirely, and the training objective collapses to a single supervised-learning expression. Just as important, because the diffusion happens directly in the state space, the policy needs only 1 denoising iteration per environment step, instead of the many iterations a typical diffusion policy runs. That is where Merlin's speed and stability come from.

zh.caption: 图2 以 2D 导航为例的前向与反向扩散过程。星号是目标状态；红色虚线箭头表示前向过程的状态转移 q(s_t|s_{t+1})，绿色箭头表示反向过程 P^{π_θ}(s_{t+1}|s_t)。策略要学的正是绿色箭头这一方向。

该往前看多远
Merlin 有两个主要的可调超参数：事后重标注的比例，以及评测时的时间视野 h（策略每一步瞄准多远的目标）。作者系统地扫描了 h 的取值，并把结果画成热力图。

zh.caption: 图5 不同评测视野 h 下各任务的相对折扣回报（左：专家数据集；右：随机数据集）。总体上「条件于某个视野」都优于「不条件」（None 列），且最优 h 随任务难度变化：简单任务偏好短视野，HandReach 尤其明显，只有在 h=1 时才表现良好。

zh.text: 从热力图可以读出两点。其一，条件于一个时间视野，几乎总是优于完全不条件（最右侧 None 列颜色更浅）。其二，最优视野取决于任务：像 PointReach 这样简单的任务，在短视野（h=1 或 h=5）下就很好，而更难的任务需要更长的视野；扫描范围大致覆盖 {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}。HandReach 是最敏感的一个——只有在 h=1 时才有效。这说明 Merlin 对视野的选择整体是稳健的，但个别高维任务仍需针对性调参。

en.subtitle: McGill and Mila propose Merlin, a value-function-free method for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 把「到达目标」看成扩散过程的逆过程
zh.subtitle: McGill 与 Mila 提出 Merlin：一个不需要价值函数的目标条件强化学习方法

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea behind Merlin. Just as image diffusion turns Gaussian noise back into a real sample, Merlin builds trajectories that walk away from the goal (grey dotted arrows, forward diffusion), then learns a goal-conditioned policy to reverse them (green solid arrows, reverse diffusion), reaching the goal from an arbitrary initial state.

en.text: Why value functions struggle here

Online reinforcement learning can keep interacting with the environment and correct a bad value estimate. Offline, it cannot: once the dataset is fixed, the agent never receives new feedback. To stabilize offline learning, prior work typically constrains the policy or uses conservative value updates, but those fixes tend to cost performance and generalization. Underneath it all is a more basic question: do we actually need to estimate how good each state is at all?

Diffusion models are a working example of an answer that says no. A forward process gradually corrupts data into Gaussian noise, and a learned reverse process denoises it back into realistic samples, without ever estimating a value function. That analogy is exactly Merlin's starting point: noise is a walk away from the data manifold, and in goal-conditioned RL we can likewise construct trajectories that walk away from a goal, then learn to reverse them.

zh.caption: 图1 本文方法 Merlin 的核心思想：正如图像扩散把高斯噪声一步步还原成真实样本，Merlin 先构造出从目标「走开」的轨迹（灰色虚线，前向扩散），再学习一个目标条件策略把它们反转（绿色实线，反向扩散），从而能从任意初始状态回到目标。

zh.text: 小结与边界
Merlin 最值得记住的一点，是它把离线目标条件强化学习重写成了一个扩散过程的逆过程，而这个重写让问题变得异常简单：构造出远离目标的轨迹、再学着反转它们，目标到达就退化成了普通的行为克隆——没有价值函数要估计，也没有随之而来的不稳定要对抗。它在 10 个任务上追平或超过当前最好的方法，却比其它扩散类方法快约一个数量级。
当然，这套框架也有它的前提。它面向的是离线、稀疏奖励、目标条件的设定；前向轨迹的构造方式（固定、参数化，或非参数拼接）需要按任务选择，个别高维任务（如 HandReach）对视野等超参数仍然敏感。但把扩散直接放在状态空间、每步只做一次去噪这一点，让「用扩散来做强化学习」第一次显得既简单又可扩展——这也许比某个具体分数更值得关注。

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea behind Merlin. Just as image diffusion turns Gaussian noise back into a real sample, Merlin builds trajectories that walk away from the goal (grey dotted arrows, forward diffusion), then learns a goal-conditioned policy to reverse them (green solid arrows, reverse diffusion), reaching the goal from an arbitrary initial state.

en.text: Takeaway and limits

The point worth remembering is that Merlin rewrites offline goal-conditioned RL as the reverse of a diffusion process, and that rewrite makes the problem remarkably simple. Construct trajectories that walk away from goals, learn to reverse them, and goal-reaching collapses into ordinary behavior cloning, with no value function to estimate and no attendant instability to fight. It matches or beats state-of-the-art methods across 10 tasks while running about an order of magnitude faster than other diffusion-based approaches.

The framework does come with conditions. It targets the offline, sparse-reward, goal-conditioned setting; the choice of forward-trajectory construction (fixed, parametric, or non-parametric stitching) has to be matched to the task, and a few high-dimensional tasks such as HandReach remain sensitive to hyperparameters like the horizon. But performing diffusion directly in the state space, with a single denoising step per environment step, is what makes diffusion for RL look, for the first time, both simple and scalable, and that may matter more than any single benchmark number.

zh.text: 效果到底如何

作者在 Yang 等人（2021）的离线目标条件基准上评测，一共 10 个控制任务，从简单的点导航、Reacher，到更难的 Fetch 抓取、推动、滑动，以及高维的 HandReach。每个任务都用稀疏二值奖励、最大轨迹长度 T=50，并在「专家」与「随机」两种数据集上、跨 10 个随机种子取平均。对比对象既包括目标条件强化学习基线（GCSL、WGCSL、AM、GoFAR），也包括扩散类方法（Decision Diffuser、g-DQL、BESO）。

zh.caption: 图4 基准任务（上）、归一化回报（左）与对数推理时间（右）。Merlin、Merlin-P、Merlin-NP（蓝色，红框标出）在回报上追平或超过所有基线，同时推理速度比扩散类方法（DD、BESO）快约一个数量级（10×）。

zh.text: 结论相当一致：最基础的 Merlin 就已经在多数任务上胜过基线，Merlin-P 与 Merlin-NP 进一步把回报推高。以在全部 10 个方法、10 个任务上的平均排名来衡量，Merlin-NP 综合最优——在状态观测下平均排名约 1.7，在像素观测下约 1.25。而由于每步只做一次去噪，它的训练和推理都比 Decision Diffuser、BESO 这类扩散方法快约 10×；观测维度越高（例如像素输入），这个速度差距还会进一步拉大。
